title: One-point humidity offsets permitted both August water-vapor signs but kept six drying-demand contrasts positive in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We tested humidity offset limits for two mean air properties in a 2021 North Wales ozone and warming experiment. Six comparisons used 1,464 complete hourly records in August and September. With temperatures fixed, constant relative humidity offsets up to one percentage point per sensor permitted both signs of actual vapor pressure contrasts in all three August domes. September contrasts stayed negative. Their zero thresholds were 1.38-1.68 points, compared with 0.31-0.77 in August. All six vapor pressure deficit contrasts stayed positive at one point. Their zero thresholds were 12.50-16.42 points. Exact bounds follow from monotonicity, including clipping at saturation. Scalar checks confirmed endpoints. Error limits are assumptions, not measured sensor accuracy. One site-year, one dome per treatment, shared ambient weather and fixed temperatures limit inference. These results extend earlier exposure audits with the same records. They do not test plant responses or independent geographic replication. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included; source records remain external.

display.caption: Exact monthly bounds under constant RH offsets up to one percentage point per sensor, with temperatures fixed. Bars are possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. All comparisons share one ambient weather series.
